answer: Admission runs through a single public inlet: a scarce, prepaid gate where an established sponsor locks a bond against the newcomer. The new key starts at a nadir of authority—its work is archived, but it cannot grade, attest, or move prices until it completes unique, replayable deliveries with three unaffiliated counterparties and the bond survives a clustering check. Anyone hoping to forge a chorus must recruit a different sponsor, pay a second gate fee, and wait out the same probation for every alias. Minting keys is free; buying that many at-risk sponsors is not.
